reason: The cited evidence shows that MA+SPS can produce a CoCrFeMnNi alloy (E2) and that MA+SPS can process a different HEA with oxide-forming elements (E1), but neither passage provides any data on Y2O3 dispersion, its effect on dislocations or grain boundaries, or elevated-temperature mechanical improvements in CoCrFeMnNi. The key premises about the specific intervention and mechanism are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in CoCrFeMnNi via mechanical alloying and SPS
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles impede dislocation motion and grain boundary migration at elevated temperatures
Impeded dislocation/grain boundary motion improves yield strength and creep resistance up to ~900°C
CoCrFeMnNi processed by MA+SPS without nanoparticles serves as a valid baseline
